items.title: Arthur "Monk" Hazel Interview, 1967-10-28
items.q: Yeah, Jimmy McPartland was the trumpet player.

ctx.x: That's the way most of the hotel bands in the old days, especially the West Coast bands and the New York bands played. Chicago mostly, they always had a little... They never put in a little jazz in there through the Dixieland, and there was a trumpet and clarinet and trombone. I was surprised when you told me who it was that was on there.
Yeah, Jimmy McPartland was the trumpet player. It was sounding good.

Yeah, Pee-wee, Pee-wee's nose, really, really russling the mind. Is he? Yeah, Pee-wee, when I first went to New York, he was doing a lot of recording with Nichols and those guys. Yeah, yeah. And then the other time, he and Bix were living together.
